hookups.source: https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/232385 (notice 'No hookups available') + catalog 232385 (all sites NONELECTRIC), read 2026-10-28

values.note: 13 reservable sites (9 RV pull-throughs, 4 tent-only) on a level open field along the inlet creek, plus 6 first-come sites on the wooded hillside above it, some walk-in (site 5 is 220 ft from parking, 7 and 8 are 180 ft). recreation.gov rates the RV sites 30-40 ft. Every vehicle must fit on the spur, no parking on the grass. Up to 8 people; one RV and two tents, or three tents, per site.

sites.source: recreation.gov catalog 232385 (13 sites: 9 STANDARD NONELECTRIC pull-through, Max Vehicle Length 30/35/40; 4 TENT ONLY) + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/232385 ('Most campsites are situated on a level, open field along a creek'; 'Six first come-first, serve-sites are perched on the wooded hillside above the creek'; FCFS notice 'Campsite #5 - 220 feet Campsite #6 - 20 feet Campsite #7 - 180 feet Campsite #8 - 180 feet'; 'all vehicles must fit in the parking spur') + https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/psicc/recreation/may-queen-campground ('A maximum of eight people and three tents or one recreational vehicle (RV) and two tents are allowed per site'), read 2026-10-28

values.note: No water in 2026; water fill-ups and trailer dumping at the Leadville Sanitation Building (the White Star and Printer Boy dump stations were closed for 2026). Trash collection; firewood $10 a bundle from the host. Hand-carried boats launch from the campground; trailered boats use the Matchless ramp.

values.note: Forest Service: 'open late May to late September, weather dependent'. Dates are recreation.gov's 2027 fee seasons (reserved May 21 - Sept 5, first-come Sept 6-18); 2026 ran May 22 - Sept 19.

season.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/psicc/recreation/may-queen-campground ('This campground is open late May to late September, weather dependent') + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/232385/rates (2027 Peak 05-21 to 09-05, First-come 09-06 to 09-18; 2026 Peak 05-22 to 09-07 and 09-08 to 09-19), read 2026-10-28

values.note: 13 sites on recreation.gov (or 877-444-6777) at least 4 days ahead; 6 hillside sites first-come, which must be occupied the first night. Friday and Saturday together on weekends, 3 nights on holiday weekends; walk-ups are exempt from the minimums. 14 consecutive nights at most. 2027 reservation season May 21 - Sept 5 (2026 ran through Sept 19).

values.note: $30 a site on recreation.gov (2026-2028) including two vehicles (an RV and its tow or towed vehicle count as one); $11 a night for a third vehicle, and boat/ATV trailers count as one. The FS page still says $29.

values.note: 50% off the site the pass holder occupies (concessionaire-run).

discounts.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/psicc/recreation/may-queen-campground ('The Interagency Senior Pass and the Interagency Access Pass qualify for a 50% discount at concessionaire-run campsites'), read 2026-10-28

note: Pike-San Isabel NF, at the far western end of Turquoise Lake near the Boustead Tunnel outlet, at ~9,900 ft in lodgepole pine beside a day-use and picnic area. The Turquoise Lake Trail runs 6.4 mi along the shore to the dam; the Timberline Lake / Colorado Trail trailhead is 1/2 mi up the road. Busy on weekends. --Claude

flags: Missing phone: Leadville Ranger District 719-486-0749 (FS page; recreation.gov lists the same, 'for information only, no reservations').
Website: recreation.gov only; add the FS page https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/psicc/recreation/may-queen-campground.

Site count: FS says 27 sites; recreation.gov's catalog lists 13 reservable (numbered 001-022 with gaps) and its text names 6 first-come hillside sites, so 19 is what can be shown. Max 40 is the catalog's largest (sites 014, 022); no agency figure.
Booking cutoff: FS says reserve 'at least four days in advance'; recreation.gov's reservationCutOff rule reads 0 ('Not Available'). Recorded the FS 4 days.
rating.price_tier 1 (RV Life, 2026-06) looks stale against the $30 fee; not changed (rating group is RV Life's).

Waterfront (stored lakefront) - re-audit lead: recreation.gov says 'Most campsites are situated on a level, open field along a creek, feeding into the lake' and the hillside sites sit 'above the creek'. On imagery with catalog points, the RV sites line the access road; the nearest (019, 020, 022) are ~55-75 m from the lake's west-end water across the road and the day-use parking, the rest ~80-150 m, with the inlet creek channel ~40-60 m SW of 010-015 and bare drawdown flats at the lake's west end. Lakefront by open apron is not shown; lakeview or creekview may fit. Not changed.

Access: PSICC alert (since April 7, 2026) barricades Turquoise Lake Road (County Road 4) 'from the Abe Lee parking turnoff to Hagerman Pass', which is recreation.gov's stated route ('head west on County Road 4 ... about 9 miles'); the alert says Turquoise Lake is still reachable 'via County Road 9C and County Road 9 to the Hagerman Pass intersection', i.e. the north-shore road to the west end.

Closure: the inclusion evidence's Willow Fire closure to 7/22/2026 has been replaced by order 02-12-01-26-39 (Oct 1 - Dec 31, 2026), which closes NFS lands south of Turquoise Lake and south of CR 4 / NFSR 105 to Busk Creek. May Queen is on the north side of the road ('on the right' heading west), so it appears outside the described area, but it sits at that area's corner; the campground season is over anyway.
Pin 39.27861,-106.43222 (= recreation.gov point) is ~117 m east of the catalog site centroid (39.27866,-106.43357); FS coordinate 39.278827,-106.43433 is ~185 m west. OK.
